_comment: THESIS-1 DONOR-KERNEL roofline vs measured (OLMo-2-7B, BF16 prefill, single socket TP=1 128c NUMA 0-2 batch 8). Same roofline-vs-measured framing as the DeepSeek (Thesis-2) charts, but reinterpreted for the REUSE leg: MEASURED = the achieved TF/s of the REUSED SGLang donor GEMM kernel wired into this model; ROOFLINE = the streamed-AMX (bandwidth) full-optimization ceiling (60.6 TF/socket). BACKEND: prefill here is M>4 so every op runs at::native::cpublas::brgemm = PyTorch ATen -> oneDNN ukernel BRGEMM (the batch-reduce GEMM building block that originated in Intel LIBXSMM; same expert lineage). The inner AMX tile loop is therefore best-in-class and NOT the bottleneck -- the GAP to the ceiling is COMPOSITION/MEMORY-TRAFFIC around brgemm (fusion, packing, prefetch, cache blocking, staging), which is exactly the Thesis-2 co-design surface. (Autoregressive decode is M<=4 and would instead use SGLang's own tinygemm intrinsic kernel, not brgemm -- an even cleaner Thesis-2 target.) The GAP = donor-kernel optimization HEADROOM, an optimization RoI that exists EVEN when no new kernel was authored. Two complementary efficiencies: eff_abs (measured/60.6, this chart) says 'is the donor kernel fully optimized?' (42-60% -> NO, headroom); eff_rel (measured vs the donor's OWN achieved on its native shape, in the note) says 'did our wiring preserve the donor's efficiency?' (0.94-1.26 -> YES). So the reuse is correct/efficient-vs-donor, yet the donor itself leaves ~40-58% on the table vs the bandwidth ceiling. Donor shapes + eff_rel from olmo2_7b_peer_roofline.json.
phase: prefill (GEMM-bound; measured = reused donor kernel; ceiling = bandwidth)
